claim: A high correlation was observed between the RUmyeloid and RUs for cHSCs in the BM.

claim: A much more consistent HSC activity was observed in-between recipients of 'pooled' cells.

claim: RUs per initial cHSC revealed 461- and 70-fold increases in PB myeloid and BM-cHSC chimerism in recipients of ex vivo expanded cells, respectively.

claim: More robustly expanding HSCs had a higher chance of reconstituting more 'daughter' recipients.

Our data agreed well with this presumption (Figure 4E), and the most actively shared clones also associated with larger outputs in 'daughter' recipients (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The most actively shared clones associated with larger outputs in 'daughter' recipients.

claim: 573 unique barcodes were recovered 16 weeks post-transplantation in the 'post-culture' setting.

claim: The median clone sizes of HSCs post-culture were significantly smaller than the pre-culture clones.

claim: The frequency of dominantly contributing clones was significantly less abundant in the 'post-culture' setting.

claim: Expanded HSCs are functionally more equivalent than input cHSCs.

claim: An average 188-fold increase of cHSCs was observed following 21 days' culture of E14.5 FL-cHSCs.

claim: Ex vivo expanded FL-cHSCs contributed considerably to multilineage reconstitution.

claim: Ex vivo expanded FL-cHSCs showed 5.7- and 6.6-fold lower reconstitution within PB myeloid cells and cHSCs when comparing to animals transplanted with cells expanded from BM-cHSCs, respectively.
